summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute on chronic left pelvic pain, consistent with prior flares. She presented with severe pain and nausea, unable to tolerate oral intake. Initial labs showed elevated lactate that improved with supportive care, and no signs of infection. Urine tests were negative for chlamydia and gonorrhea. She was restarted on her home pain regimen, including gabapentin, ibuprofen, and tramadol, and received IV fluids for dehydration. Her hemoglobin declined to 9.9 g/dL, reflecting ongoing anemia likely due to menorrhagia, and outpatient colonoscopy was scheduled to evaluate for rectal endometriosis. Lithium level was therapeutic, and subclinical hypothyroidism was noted but not treated. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up plans in gynecology and for surgical evaluation.
